story.c00.b00.heard: Two taps. That's me. If you're hearing this, I missed a check-in, and you're sitting in my chair because nobody else wanted the paperwork.

story.c00.b01.heard: He missed three. He told me once, one check-in is weather, two is trouble, three is worry. I've been worried since Tuesday.

story.c00.b02.heard: Sparrow, you fly the pattern too low and too fast, and I never fixed it because it's the only thing you do without asking permission.

story.c00.b03.heard: Command calls it desertion. They made me say the word on the net. I said it. I'm not saying it again.

story.c00.b04.heard: If I miss your checkout, fly the pattern anyway. The sky will still be there.

story.c00.b05.heard: An empty chair and a checkout nobody's signing. Fine, I'll fly the pattern.

story.c01.b00.heard: The bombers wore our markings, our paint, our numbers. One of them was a tail I cleared for departure in March.

story.c01.b01.heard: The quartermaster found a case under Teal's bunk, a coffee tin, twelve tapes, and a note, "For Sarah, not for the net."

story.c01.b02.heard: Keep these off the command net. Somebody up there is listening and signing things they shouldn't. If I go quiet, the case goes to Sarah, only Sarah.

story.c01.b03.heard: The manifest sends grain drums to a farm with a runway, then five keys on Iron Coast. Nobody ships grain in drums.

story.c01.b04.heard: There are real houses in that yard, families who work the siding. I need you to come home with the right number of fires.

story.c01.b05.heard: Iron Coast is a hundred miles of our own shoreline. Whoever this is, they're not invading. They're already home.

story.c01.b06.heard: Then I'll look at that farm from above before anyone can tidy it up.

story.c02.b00.heard: I dropped beacons on the way in, low power, my own frequency. If anyone ever follows me, I wanted it to be someone who knew the song.

story.c02.b01.heard: He used to tune that pass on Sundays, said it was the only place the tower couldn't talk to him.

story.c02.b02.heard: Recovery followed the beacons into the snowy pass. His receiver was in the rocks. Cracked case, memory intact. He meant us to find it.

story.c02.b03.heard: There's a radar inside our own training box dug into the bowl north of the pass. Nobody signed for it. I checked the ledger three times.

story.c02.b04.heard: Somebody wanted to watch trainees, not the sky. Trainees. Think about why you'd want to know when the kids fly.

story.c02.b05.heard: If it's real, it's been watching every pattern you've flown for a year. Command wants it gone quietly. I want it photographed first.

story.c02.b06.heard: If I just blow it up, it's a rumor. If I look at it first, it's a crime.

story.c03.b00.heard: The tech land farmers let me hide a tape in a seed tin. The old woman asked my name, not my rank. Nobody at Varda has asked my name in ten years.

story.c03.b01.heard: The radar's memory names that orchard. Three days later, somebody ordered it evacuated. Now, there are patrols firing on the evacuation trucks.

story.c03.b02.heard: They're not shooting at farmers. They're shooting at a seed tin. That's how badly someone wants Teal's tape back.

story.c03.b03.heard: Three officers at Varda are being reassigned tonight. Their names are already off the roster. Nobody will ask. Nobody ever asks.

story.c03.b04.heard: The couriers carry patrol routes high over the orchard hills. Their crews guide the guns onto the trucks.

story.c03.b05.heard: Three transports above the hills with escorts hidden by two jammers. Find the transports, and the families have a road out.

story.c03.b06.heard: Those trucks are carrying somebody who asked his name. They get out.

story.c04.b00.heard: The convoy made it. The old woman's granddaughter drove the lead truck. She marked three silos on the map with her thumb. Those smell wrong.

story.c04.b01.heard: Three tanks under grain permits, aviation fuel. The farmers know the difference. They just can't prove it. A fuel ledger would prove it.

story.c04.b02.heard: Sparrow, every unmarked silo in that valley is somebody's winter. Don't be the one who makes them hungry to make a point.

story.c04.b03.heard: He wrote that one for you. He never wrote anything for me. I'm choosing not to be hurt by that today.

story.c04.b04.heard: Vulture lead followed me into the pass. He wasn't chasing a deserter. You don't chase deserters at night with your lights off. He was erasing a witness.

story.c04.b05.heard: If the fuel burns, he'll come looking for you over the works. You don't owe him a duel. Bring yourself home.

story.c04.b06.heard: Three thumbprints, three fires, then I'm leaving him in the dark.

story.c05.b00.heard: You got clear of Vulture lead. His orders kept repeating on guard. We recorded them. Every one bears a governor's name. He died in spring.

story.c05.b01.heard: Kiro talks to Lira. Lira talks to Meril. Meril talks to the harbors. Start at the keys. Listen back up the chain.

story.c05.b02.heard: I wiped his name off my board this morning, then I wrote it back. I'm not ready to decide what he is.

story.c05.b03.heard: On the coast, look at what the cranes unload. The uniforms tell you nothing. The crates do.

story.c05.b04.heard: Iron Coast, military stores beside a fish market. The marshal put his war where he knew we'd hesitate.

story.c05.b05.heard: Workers are two blocks from those keys. The ships and tankers are his supply line. Their neighbors are not.

story.c05.b06.heard: He's right. I'll hesitate, then I'll aim.

story.c06.b00.heard: Kiro keeps an archive, every forged order filed because forgers are vain. It's the only honest thing on the plateau.

story.c06.b01.heard: Declare the emergency first. Find the reason after. In a year, nobody has asked me for the reason.

story.c06.b02.heard: The harbor traffic gave us Kiro's signing key. A key alone is a rumor. We need Lira and Meril's logs with the same signature.

story.c06.b03.heard: Lira and Meril sit on opposite ridges and hate each other's weather. Lira lies, Meril repeats her. The west ridge still hears the farms.

story.c06.b04.heard: Three logs, one signature. Send them home to Varda. Its island transmitter can reach the farms without borrowing his voice.

story.c06.b05.heard: I came home through the pass, not the pretty way, the way you take when you don't want to be seen coming home.

story.c06.b06.heard: His own words, in his own voice, on their own relay. He'd have liked that.

story.c07.b00.heard: Three stations, one signature. Varda's island transmitter has the orders and the governor's death certificate, thirty-five seconds.

story.c07.b01.heard: A clear signal needs time. Don't give them a hero. Give them thirty-five seconds, and a hero is beside the point.

story.c07.b02.heard: He recorded that two weeks before he vanished. Thirty-five seconds. He'd already timed it. He knew exactly what this would take.

story.c07.b03.heard: I'm staying in the tower, in case you were wondering. I'm not leaving my chair for them.

story.c07.b04.heard: Keep the lights on, Sarah. I'll keep the sky.

story.c08.b00.heard: Three garrisons heard it. Two stood down. Their people are coming ashore to join us.

story.c08.b01.heard: Three loyalist frigates cover the landing under the weather. The command ship carries a green beacon and most of our hope.

story.c08.b02.heard: Storms ground frightened people. They don't ground orders or fuel or the people who own them. When the weather's bad, that's when they move.

story.c08.b03.heard: If I don't get home, leave the lane open for the next one. That's the job. There isn't a second part.

story.c08.b04.heard: The frigate captain was at his wing ceremony. Half this coast was. The marshal forgot that we all remember.

story.c08.b05.heard: Green beacon. I'll stay close enough to read it.

story.c09.b00.heard: And then the marshal answered, "Fire at the orchard, a line of guns along the rivers."

story.c09.b01.heard: Varda Rim has broadcast enemy propaganda. It is a hostile station. The Tecklan Orchard sheltered the source. There will be no further warnings.

story.c09.b02.heard: The orchard burned at noon. The old woman is alive. Her granddaughter is alive. The seed tin is ash. That's my report, and I hate it.

story.c09.b03.heard: I asked you to broadcast. I'd ask again. I need you to know that I'd ask again.

story.c09.b04.heard: The rain has passed. The line hasn't. I'll take the valleys.

story.c10.b00.heard: The old woman heard Teal in her kitchen before the fire. She says he sounded tired. Now her neighbors are flying out over his saddle.

story.c10.b01.heard: Teal flew that saddle on his check ride. Vulture Two signed the card. I pulled it last night. The handwriting matches the forged orders.

story.c10.b02.heard: Two civilian airliners, one cannot climb. Somebody will have to leave the high sky to keep the lower one safe.

story.c10.b03.heard: Then I'll fly his check ride for him, properly this time.

story.c11.b00.heard: The eight towers in that crater are the marshal's command array. The antennas up there are his. So is the pilot waiting above them.

story.c11.b01.heard: Varda trainee, this is Vulture Two. I taught your instructor to fly. I know what he'd try over that crater. Turn home. Nobody has to watch.

story.c11.b02.heard: Vulture Two taught me that an order is not the same as a duty, then he forgot. If you meet him, remind him loudly.

story.c11.b03.heard: He's challenged your call sign in daylight. He wants you above the crater where he can see your face.

story.c11.b04.heard: If he ejects, mark where he lands. We need a witness who can answer back.

story.c12.b00.heard: Vulture Two ejected. Marines lifted him out of the crater. He asked if you were Teal's. I said, "Yes."

story.c12.b01.heard: He was the best I ever signed off. Tell the kid the handwriting was mine, all of it. I'm done lying to pilots.

story.c12.b02.heard: I made a paper copy. Radios get jammed. Ink still travels. It's in the harbor master's safe, and she doesn't like the marshal either.

story.c12.b03.heard: The harbor master's copy and Vulture Two's statement are on one slow plane. Airships are jamming the ravine. Fighters are waiting beyond it.

story.c12.b04.heard: The signatures, his tapes, a living witness on paper. If that plane falls, command gets to call him a deserter again.

story.c13.b00.heard: The evidence plane is clear. Its papers point to the crown station on the ice coast. Missiles are closing on the dish. We need its archive intact.

story.c13.b01.heard: At the crown station, I left the order that started all of this, the first one, with his real signature before he learned to use dead men's names.

story.c13.b02.heard: I didn't take it with me. I didn't trust myself to get home. I trusted the dish.

story.c13.b03.heard: He didn't trust himself to get home. He said it out loud to a tape and flew anyway. I keep rewinding that part.

story.c13.b04.heard: He trusted the dish. I can do that much.

story.c14.b00.heard: Archive recovered. Order zero zero zero one: Declare regional emergency. Suspend Parliament. Assume air command. Signed, Rusk, Air Marshal.

story.c14.b01.heard: Rusk, he gave the speech at Teal's wing ceremony. He told us the sky belongs to whoever is willing to be up in it.

story.c14.b02.heard: Marines have the paper copy. Now the archive gives us his signature too, and the city still hears nothing but him.

story.c14.b03.heard: Citizens, Parliament has fled. Rebel aircraft are over the harbor. Stay inside. Trust the lights. Trust my voice.

story.c14.b04.heard: One tower, one voice, one emergency on repeat. He didn't build it to tell anyone anything. He built it so nothing else gets in.

story.c14.b05.heard: The broadcast relay sits in a block of apartments. He chose that too. The canal is the only dark line through the city.

story.c14.b06.heard: Everyone in those apartments has been listening to him for a year. I'd like to give them some quiet.

story.c15.b00.heard: Trainee, this is Rusk. Teal flew my wing the winter the coast starved while Parliament debated. He had talent too. Ask the pass how far it got him.

story.c15.b01.heard: That's the first time he's used his own name. He wants you to know he's a person. Don't let him.

story.c15.b02.heard: He flew your wing. Vulture lead hunted him for you. I'll remember who gave the order.

story.c15.b03.heard: A loyalist column is crossing the dry coast. Parliament is coming home by road. The ruined town ahead of them still has guns.

story.c15.b04.heard: Don't fly for the people giving orders. Fly for the people who have to live beneath them. The man on the net is weather.

story.c15.b05.heard: He recorded that one at two in the morning. I can hear the hangar heater behind him. I could find that hangar in the dark by that sound.

story.c15.b06.heard: Clear the bunkers ahead of the column. Stay on their channel until both squads answer from the streets.

story.c15.b07.heard: Beneath them. Right. The road then.

story.c16.b00.heard: Recovery reached the upper pass this morning. They found his aircraft. They found him. He was in the seat. The recorder was still running.

story.c16.b01.heard: Recorder 7T, entry oh four twelve. Playback.

story.c16.b02.heard: Two taps. Sparrow, it's me. Lead is on my tail, and I'm out of altitude, so I'm going to stay in the pass a while. The seed trucks need ten minutes.

story.c16.b03.heard: I flew that order knowing the price. The tapes are so you never have to take my word for any of it. This part I'm choosing myself.

story.c16.b04.heard: Fly the pattern too low and too fast. Nobody ever fixed it. Good. The sky will-

story.c16.b05.heard: Witnesses reach Parliament tonight. Keep the bridges and key open. Rusk leads four wingmen over the capital. Vulture lead is one of them.

story.c16.b06.heard: I've amended the record myself. Aircraft lost with pilot, killed, not deserted. Command can court-martial the paperwork.

story.c16.b07.heard: Ten minutes. He bought ten minutes. I'm going to go and spend them.

story.c17.b00.heard: The wing is broken. Rusk left his wingmen and ran to the coastal relay works. He's alone there with one relay and his own voice.

story.c17.b01.heard: Trainee, land, and I'll tell the city you were misled by a dead man. Fly, and you're the traitor in every history I write.

story.c17.b02.heard: When you have the truth, send it in your own voice. You don't have to sound like me. You never did.

story.c17.b03.heard: I've got every harbor on the net. Every loyalist station is listening for one call sign, not his, yours.

story.c17.b04.heard: Break the generators, run the vent, and get clear. When his loop stops, he'll come up alone. Then the sky is yours to answer him.

story.c17.b05.heard: Marshal, I heard the tape. He didn't sound misled. He sounded like he was counting trucks.

story.c17.b06.heard: Sarah, Varda trainee checking in. One of three. The other two are for after.

story.c18.b00.heard: He's down. His relay is dark. Every harbor on the coast is answering. You're on every receiver from the Rim to the sea. Say it your way.

story.c18.b01.heard: This is Varda trainee transmitting in the clear. The Air Marshal is down. The emergency is over. It never started.

story.c18.b02.heard: The orders were forged. The names were dead men's. An orchard was burned for a seed tin. Teal flew the pass so the trucks could get out.

story.c18.b03.heard: His name was Teal. He was not a deserter. Amend your records. For Teal, for the Rim, we are coming home.

story.c18.b04.heard: Varda trainee, Varda control. Check-in received, two of three. Come home and make the third in person.

story.c18.b05.heard: The sky will still be there.

story.c18.b06.heard: Varda Rim roster. Teal killed in action, not deserted. Instructor's chair filled.

radio.m04.story.1.heard: High contacts are guiding the patrols. The trucks need that sky clear.

radio.m04.story.2.heard: The road is open. Count the trucks at Varda.

radio.m05.story.1.heard: Fuel tanks only. The grain silos beside them feed families.

radio.m05.story.2.heard: Vulture flight inbound. Leave the works. Survive. This is no duel.

radio.m05.story.3.heard: You are clear. I kept his orders on tape.

radio.m06.story.1.heard: Iron Coast ahead. Ships and tankers, leave the market clear.

radio.m06.story.2.heard: Harbor traffic copied. We can follow the orders inland.

radio.m07.story.1.heard: Copy before you cut. We need the signature, not just wreckage.

radio.m07.story.2.heard: Guns have the ridge. Take the canyon.

radio.m08.story.1.heard: I am staying in the tower. Keep the bombers away from the transmitter.

radio.m08.story.2.heard: Thirty-five seconds sent. Two garrisons are answering.

radio.m09.story.1.heard: Green beacon is ours. Clear the guns above the beach.

radio.m09.story.2.heard: The landing is through. There is smoke over Teclin.

radio.m10.story.1.heard: Keep the valley between you and the long-range guns.

radio.m10.story.2.heard: The corridor is open. Two civilian flights are ready.

radio.m11.story.1.heard: One airliner cannot climb. Watch both altitude bands.

radio.m11.story.2.heard: Both flights are clear. I have a name for that handwriting.

radio.m12.story.1.heard: Eight towers. The command array is his. The crater is your way in.

radio.m13.story.1.heard: Jammers in the ravine. Clear the plane a channel.

radio.m13.story.2.heard: Fighters beyond the fog. Keep them off the evidence plane.

radio.m14.story.1.heard: Missiles low over the ice. The dish must keep talking.

radio.m14.story.2.heard: Archive received. Order zero-zero-zero one, Rusk.

radio.m15.story.1.heard: Loyalist troops below. Keep Rusk's armor off their streets.

radio.m15.story.2.heard: Bombers incoming. They are turning on the city.

radio.m16.story.1.heard: Clear the bunkers ahead of the column.

radio.m16.story.2.heard: Both squads answering from the streets. Parliament has a road home.

radio.m17.story.1.heard: Rusk leads four wingmen. Vulture lead is back over the capital.

radio.m17.story.2.heard: He left his wing. Rusk is running for the coast.

radio.m18.story.1.heard: Generators first, then the central vent. Leave yourself a way out.

radio.m18.story.2.heard: You are clear. His loop has stopped. Rusk is coming up alone.

radio.m01.p1.beat.heard: Six bombers are paint and codes. Stop them before the North Coast.

radio.m02.p1.beat.heard: Follow the power line north. Their bombers are parked on the farm.

radio.m02.p1.chatter1.heard: Bombers, start engines. Get them off the ground.

radio.m02.p1.chatter2.heard: Four down. Their guns are still up. Watch the base edges.

radio.m02.p1.chatter3.heard: The pads are burning. Nobody takes off from here.

radio.m02.p1.chatter4.heard: One bomber left. Finish it, trainee.

radio.m03.p1.beat.heard: Enemy airspace. Site one is on the ridge northwest of you.

radio.m03.p1.chatter2.heard: Five domes down. Site two is on the saddle west-northwest.

radio.m03.p1.chatter3.heard: One dome left. Finish it and we go home.

radio.m03.p3.landing1.heard: Trainee, gear check. Cleared to land, runway three-six.

radio.m03.p3.landing2.heard: Runway in sight. You're on the center line.

radio.m03.p3.landing3.heard: Short final. Glide path is good. Hold it there.

radio.m03.p3.landing5.heard: Welcome home. Sarah wants that film before you unstrap.
